sections.html:
Bills come from Pierce County. Tacoma is the county seat, and the county's Assessor-Treasurer's Office values each house and also collects the money.

  • Pay or check a balance in person: Pierce County Annex, 2401 S 35th Street, Room 142, Tacoma. A drop box serves after-hours payments.
  • Customer service: (253) 798-6111.
  • Automated tax and value line: (253) 798-3333. With a parcel number it takes card and e-check payments.
  • Foreclosure avoidance payments: send a cashier's check to Pierce County marked Attention: Foreclosure Avoidance, at the Room 142 address.

The city's own levy is folded into one combined rate. Statements go out in February and the county collects the whole amount.

Tacoma is a port city on Puget Sound, roughly 30 miles from Seattle and from Olympia, with 229,816 residents in July 2025 on 49.71 square miles. Owners occupy 55.8 percent of homes, and the median value of an owned home is $479,600. Median gross rent is $1,676 and median household income is $85,884.

Roughly 44 percent of Tacoma households rent, and that is a fact to weigh before you list. If the house you are selling has a tenant, plan for that in your timeline, because tax bills and sale paperwork still run through you as the owner of record.

Owners pay one half by April 30 and the second half by October 31. Statements arrive in February. A bill of $50 or less is paid whole on April 30. A statement that never showed up is no excuse, and interest still builds.

Mail the check so the postmark falls on or before the deadline. The county suggests certified mail with a return receipt, so you hold proof of the mailing date, and it will forgive interest when the postmark shows you mailed in time. If a check comes in late and short on the right interest, it is returned. Lenders live by the same calendar as individual owners and are expected to pay every tax, assessment and charge on the parcel.

The county prints your parcel number, the value used and each district's levy on the statement. Keep that statement with your sale paperwork, since the title company will ask for the parcel number and for proof of what has been paid. If the statement is lost, call the same number for a copy.

Behind on the second half? Call (253) 798-6111 for your balance and any interest already running.

sections.h2: What is the Tacoma tax rate?
sections.html:
For 2026, Pierce County puts the average rate in Tacoma's tax code area 005 at $10.876 per $1,000 of assessed value. That single figure covers every taxing district stacked on the area. Individual parcels can drift a little from the average, so read the rate on your own statement.

The assessor looks at sales made before January 1 and values every parcel as of that day. The 2026 assessment therefore reflects 2025 sales, and it forms the base for taxes due in 2027. The county explains the yearly calendar on its residential appeals page.

sections.h2: If you fall behind on Tacoma property tax
sections.html:
For a residential property with one to four units and tax year 2023 or later, interest is 0.75 percent per month on the full year's tax from May 1. Penalties of 3 percent and 8 percent are charged on other property types, so a single-family house does not collect them. Monthly payment plans are offered by the Assessor-Treasurer:

  • A plan for current tax through escrow costs $100 to set up and $15 a month.
  • A plan for delinquent tax costs $100 to set up and $17 a month, and it can run up to 18 months.
  • The oldest unpaid tax has to be cleared in full by April 30 of the year it turns three years delinquent.

Foreclosure comes next. Parcels with more than $100 in cumulative tax that is three or more years delinquent are foreclosed through a Certificate of Delinquency filed in Pierce County Superior Court. To ask about a plan, call (253) 798-2728.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Tacoma property value?
sections.html:
The Pierce County Board of Equalization takes petitions filed by July 1 or within 60 days after your value change notice was mailed. It accepts only the Department of Revenue petition form, one parcel per form.

  • Hearings turn on what the house was worth on January 1. The size of the bill, a big percentage jump, what neighbors pay and your finances are all off the table.
  • Good evidence includes comparable sales from the right year, contractor bids to fix defects, easement documents, independent appraisals and photographs.
  • A petition that merely says the value or tax is too high is rejected.
  • Late exhibits are due 21 business days ahead of the hearing.

The county's value is presumed correct, which puts the burden of proof on you. The board's office is at 2401 S 35th St, Room 176, phone (253) 798-7415. RCW 84.40.038 sets the baseline deadlines and spells out good-cause reasons for accepting a late petition.

Seniors and people with disabilities may apply for an exemption that can freeze taxable value and remove certain levies. You qualify if you are at least 61 or have been awarded disability status by December 31 of the previous year, earn no more than $64,000 after allowable deductions, own the home by December 31 of the assessment year, and live in it more than six months of the prior year. An application is required.

Excise tax on the sale is billed apart from property tax. The state rate climbs with the price:

Sale priceState excise rate
Sales up to $525,0001.1 percent
Between $525,000.01 and $1,525,0001.28 percent
Between $1,525,000.01 and $3,025,0002.75 percent
Above $3,025,0003 percent

These are the rates for sales on or after January 1, 2023, and Tacoma adds a 0.50 percent local rate. Property tax itself is prorated by sale date under RCW 84.60.020, with the lien attaching each January 1. Have your escrow officer confirm the open half with the Assessor-Treasurer.

Do this homework before the listing goes live so tax questions do not stall escrow.

  • Look up the parcel number and check what the automated line at (253) 798-3333 shows as owed.
  • Check whether the fall half is paid, and if not, get the exact interest to date.
  • If you are on a payment plan, tell escrow so the remaining balance is cleared from proceeds.
  • If you hold a senior or disability exemption, confirm with the Assessor-Treasurer what changes when ownership transfers.
  • If a tenant lives in the house, work out the showing schedule before you list.

Sellers who need a fast close sometimes choose a cash buyer, which skips the appraisal and lender review. Any tax owed still comes out of the proceeds, so you need the payoff number regardless of who buys.

faqs.q: Who do I pay Tacoma property tax to?
faqs.a: Pierce County's Assessor-Treasurer, not the city. Options are the website, the phone line at (253) 798-3333, a mailed check to Pierce County Finance, or the counter at 2401 S 35th Street, Room 142. Checks are made out to Pierce County.

faqs.q: What is the interest on late Tacoma property tax?
faqs.a: On a home of four or fewer units, 0.75 percent a month on the full year's tax from May 1, for tax year 2023 and later. The 3 and 8 percent penalties apply to other property types.

faqs.q: How long can Tacoma property tax go unpaid before foreclosure?
faqs.a: Three years. Pierce County forecloses on parcels with more than $100 in cumulative tax that is three or more years delinquent.

faqs.q: When must I file a Tacoma assessment appeal?
faqs.a: The county board wants your petition by July 1 of the assessment year, or 60 days after your value change notice was mailed. Attach a copy of that notice if you file after July 1.

faqs.q: Is there excise tax on a Tacoma home sale?
faqs.a: Yes. The state graduated excise rate applies to the sale, and Tacoma adds a 0.50 percent local rate. Your escrow officer can give the exact figure at your sale price.
